newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Digicall shares dive on warning.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Digicall shares dive on warning.

text.p: Shares in mobile telcommunications reseller Digicall Group Ltd dived over 30 percent after the company said its earnings to June 30 would be adversely impacted by inactive and unviable subscribers.
By 3.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), Digicall shares were 12.5 cents lower at 25 cents on turnover of 218,700 shares.

Earlier on Monday, the company said a recent review of its business had identified a significant block of inactive or unviable subscribers and the company was now taking action to recover outstanding debts, bar or re-tariff these customers.
The company estimated that as a result of its subscriber base clean-up, there would be no net growth in its digital subscriber base in the quarter ending September 30, 1996.
"Whilst the remaining subscribers will represent a quality base, the above actions will adversely impact the company's results for the year ended June 30, 1996," Digicall said.
Digicall said it estimated its bad debts to be in the region of A$11 million at June 30, 1996 with only A$2 million provided for in the half year accounts to December 31, 1995.
Digicall said discussions were now in progress with a number of telephone comapanies including Vodafone regarding future funding for Digicall's business.
Digical shares closed 12.5 cents lower at 25 cents on turnover of 275,900 shares.
